definition_en: to state something clearly and exactly, or to name it as a requirement
core_image: 表格上的一栏被红笔圈出，旁边写着必须填写的具体内容
scene: 请在表格上注明你到达的日期。Please specify the date of your arrival on the form.
sceneCN: 这里 specify 是「明确说明、注明」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请在表格上注明你到达的日期。

senses.title: To state exactly
senses.definition: to say something clearly so there is no doubt
senses.definitionCN: 清楚说出，使人没有疑问
senses.example: Please specify the date of your arrival on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 请在表格上注明你到达的日期。
senses.why: This is the central modern sense of naming details exactly.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代表示确切说明细节的核心含义。

senses.title: To set as a rule
senses.definition: to state something as a required condition
senses.definitionCN: 把某事作为必要条件加以规定
senses.example: The contract specifies a two-week notice period.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定了两周的通知期。
senses.why: A stated detail becomes a rule when it is written down.
senses.whyCN: 写下来的细节，就成了规定。

senses.title: To mark on a label
senses.definition: to state something on a product or document
senses.definitionCN: 在产品或文件上写明
senses.example: Each box must specify its weight.
senses.exampleCN: 每个箱子上都必须注明重量。
senses.why: A label that names its contents specifies them.
senses.whyCN: 写明内容的标签，就是在注明。

intro.en: Specify came from medieval Latin specificare, to name by kind.
intro.cn: specify 来自中世纪拉丁语 specificare，意为按种类指明。

items.en: Species meant kind or appearance.
items.cn: species 意为种类或外观。

items.en: Specificare meant to name a thing by its kind.
items.cn: specificare 意为按种类指明事物。

items.en: Specify entered English meaning to state in detail.
items.cn: specify 以详述之义进入英语。

items.en: Contracts used it for required conditions.
items.cn: 合同用它表示必要条件。

items.en: Labels used it for weights and contents.
items.cn: 标签用它标注重量和内容。

note.en: Specify is compared with look-alike words and verbs of stating.
note.cn: 把 specify 与形近词以及表示陈述的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To specify is to point with words until nothing is vague.
normalIntro.cn: specify 就是用词语指到不再含糊为止。

normal.en: Please specify the date of your arrival on the form.
normal.cn: 请在表格上注明你到达的日期。

normal.en: The contract specifies a two-week notice period.
normal.cn: 合同规定了两周的通知期。

normal.en: Each box must specify its weight.
normal.cn: 每个箱子上都必须注明重量。

normal.en: The rules clearly specify what is allowed.
normal.cn: 规则明确说明了允许的范围。

normal.en: Unless otherwise specified, all prices include tax.
normal.cn: 除非另有说明，所有价格都含税。

abstract.en: A vague wish cannot be carried out.
abstract.cn: 含糊的愿望无法被执行。

abstract.en: To name the detail is to take half the action.
abstract.cn: 点明细节，就等于完成了行动的一半。

abstract.en: What is left unspecified will be argued over.
abstract.cn: 没有说明的部分，终将引起争论。

examples.cn: 请在表格上注明你到达的日期。

examples.cn: 合同规定了两周的通知期。

examples.en: Each box must specify its weight.
examples.cn: 每个箱子上都必须注明重量。

dict_mnemonic.text: specify 源自拉丁语 species（种类），表示「按种类指明」，即明确说明、指定、注明；specific 是「具体的」，specifically 是「具体地」，specification 是「规格、详细说明」。

root: 来自中世纪拉丁语 specificare（按种类指明），源于 species（种类、外观），核心义为把事物具体指名，使其不再含糊。

sensesIntro.en: Specify means to state something exactly, to set it as a requirement, or to mark it on a label.

core.en: Naming the exact point of a thing.
core.cn: 点出事物确切的那一点。

branches.en: A blank form asks for one exact date.
branches.cn: 一张空白表格要求一个确切日期。

branches.en: A contract fixes the notice period in writing.
branches.cn: 合同以书面固定通知期。

branches.en: A box is marked with its weight.
branches.cn: 箱子上标着重量。

branches.en: Stating a detail can turn it into a rule.
branches.cn: 说明一个细节，就能把它变成规则。

branches.en: Contracts and labels both put exact words on record.
branches.cn: 合同与标签都把确切的词语留在记录里。

intro.en: Specify forms nouns and adjectives of exact statement.
intro.cn: specify 构成表示确切陈述的名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is specificare, to name by kind, from species, a kind.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 specificare（按种类指明），源于 species（种类）。

items.exampleCN: 这本书是专为初学者写的。

definition_en: a small part or example of something kept or tested to show what the whole is like
core_image: 玻璃罐里泡着一片叶子，标签上写着采集地点与日期
scene: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
sceneCN: 这里 specimen 是「标本」（第 1 个义项）；句意：科学家把一片叶子做成标本。

senses.title: A kept example
senses.definition: a part of a plant or animal kept for study
senses.definitionCN: 保存下来供研究的动植物部分
senses.example: The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。
senses.why: This is the museum and laboratory sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是博物馆和实验室里的含义。

senses.title: A sample for testing
senses.definition: a small amount taken to be tested or examined
senses.definitionCN: 取出用于检测或检查的少量物质
senses.example: The lab tested a blood specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室检测了一份血液样本。
senses.why: Anything taken for testing acts as a specimen.
senses.whyCN: 任何取出供检测的东西都充当样本。

senses.title: A type of person
senses.definition: a person considered as an example of a kind, often humorously
senses.definitionCN: 作为某类范例的人，常带幽默意味
senses.example: The coach called him a fine specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称他是个体格健壮的好苗子。
senses.why: Informal speech treats a strong person like a fine sample.
senses.whyCN: 口语把强壮的人比作上好的样本。

intro.en: Specimen is Latin for a mark or sample, from the verb to look.
intro.cn: specimen 是拉丁语中表示标记或样品的词，源于表示看的动词。

items.en: Specere meant to look or observe.
items.cn: specere 意为看或观察。

items.en: Specimen meant a mark or a sample to look at.
items.cn: specimen 意为标记或供观察的样品。

items.en: Specimen entered English as a sample for study.
items.cn: specimen 以研究样本之义进入英语。

items.en: Museums kept plant and animal specimens.
items.cn: 博物馆保存动植物标本。

items.en: Medicine took specimens for testing.
items.cn: 医学取样本进行检测。

note.en: Specimen is compared with look-alike words and words for samples.
note.cn: 把 specimen 与形近词以及表示样品的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small part taken as an example
one thing that shows a group

normalIntro.en: A specimen is a small piece kept so that others can look closely.
normalIntro.cn: specimen 是保留下来的小块，供人仔细观看。

normal.en: The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
normal.cn: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。

normal.en: The lab tested a blood specimen.
normal.cn: 实验室检测了一份血液样本。

normal.en: The coach called him a fine specimen.

normal.cn: 博物馆把稀有标本保存在玻璃柜里。

normal.en: She collected plant specimens on the walk.
normal.cn: 她在散步时采集了植物标本。

abstract.en: A specimen is a part that agrees to speak for the whole.
abstract.cn: 标本是愿意替整体发言的一部分。

abstract.en: To study a leaf is to question the forest.
abstract.cn: 研究一片叶子，就是在追问整片森林。

abstract.en: What is kept in glass is kept from living.
abstract.cn: 封在玻璃里的，也被挡在生命之外。

examples.cn: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。

examples.cn: 教练称他是个体格健壮的好苗子。

dict_mnemonic.text: specimen 源自拉丁语 specere（看），指供观察研究的「标本、样本」；复数 specimens，blood specimen 是「血液样本」，specimen collection 是「标本收藏」，同根词有 species、specific、specify。

root: 来自拉丁语 specimen（标记、样品），源于 specere（看），本义为供人观察的东西，后指动植物标本、检测样本与某种类型的人。

sensesIntro.en: Specimen means a part kept for study, a sample for testing, or informally a type of person.

core.en: A small piece offered to the eye.

branches.en: A leaf floats in a labelled jar.
branches.cn: 一片叶子浮在贴着标签的罐子里。

branches.en: A tube of blood goes to the lab.
branches.cn: 一管血被送往实验室。

branches.en: A strong young man is praised by his coach.
branches.cn: 教练称赞一个健壮的年轻人。

branches.en: Museum and laboratory both study small parts.
branches.cn: 博物馆与实验室都研究小部分。

branches.cn: 检测样本与人的样本，共享一个意象。

definition_en: extremely impressive to look at, or surprisingly great
core_image: 烟花在河面上空同时炸开，光映在成千上万张仰起的脸上
scene: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
sceneCN: 这里 spectacular 是「壮观的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。

senses.title: Impressive to see
senses.definition: extremely impressive or beautiful to look at
senses.definitionCN: 看上去极其壮观或美丽
senses.example: Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
senses.exampleCN: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。
senses.why: This is the central sense of a sight worth watching.
senses.whyCN: 这是值得观看的景象的核心含义。

senses.title: Surprisingly great
senses.definition: surprisingly large or successful
senses.definitionCN: 大得或成功得出人意料
senses.example: The team made a spectacular comeback.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍实现了惊人的逆转。
senses.why: A result can be as striking as a show.
senses.whyCN: 结果也能像表演一样引人注目。

senses.title: A brilliant show
senses.definition: very exciting and well done, as a performance
senses.definitionCN: 表演非常激动人心、完成得出色
senses.example: The show ended with a spectacular finale.
senses.exampleCN: 演出以精彩的终场结束。
senses.why: The theatre gave the word its sense of a great show.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧赋予这个词「精彩演出」的含义。

intro.en: Spectacular came from Latin spectare, to look at, through spectaculum, a show.
intro.cn: spectacular 来自拉丁语 spectare（观看），经 spectaculum（表演）而来。

items.en: Spectare meant to look at or watch.
items.cn: spectare 意为观看、注视。

items.en: Spectaculum meant a show or a sight.
items.cn: spectaculum 意为表演或景象。

items.en: Spectacular entered English meaning of a show.
items.cn: spectacular 以「表演的」之义进入英语。

items.en: It spread to views and natural scenery.
items.cn: 它扩展到景色和自然风光。

items.en: It came to describe surprising success or failure.
items.cn: 它逐渐用来形容惊人的成功或失败。

note.en: Spectacular is compared with look-alike words and words for magnificence.
note.cn: 把 spectacular 与形近词以及表示壮丽的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spectacular is a sight that makes the crowd look up and forget itself.
normalIntro.cn: spectacular 是让人群抬头、忘掉自己的景象。

normal.en: Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
normal.cn: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。

normal.en: The team made a spectacular comeback.
normal.cn: 这支队伍实现了惊人的逆转。

normal.en: The show ended with a spectacular finale.
normal.cn: 演出以精彩的终场结束。

normal.en: The mountain road offers a spectacular view.
Her first novel was a spectacular success.
normal.cn: 她的第一部小说获得了惊人的成功。

abstract.en: A spectacle is a sight that charges admission to the heart.
abstract.cn: 奇观是向心脏收费的景象。

abstract.en: What is spectacular soon becomes ordinary.
abstract.cn: 壮观的景象，很快就会变得平常。

abstract.en: The greatest shows leave silence behind.
abstract.cn: 最盛大的演出，留下的是寂静。

examples.en: Fireworks burst over the river in a spectacular display.
examples.cn: 烟花在河面上空绽放，景象十分壮观。

examples.en: The team made a spectacular comeback.
examples.cn: 这支队伍实现了惊人的逆转。

examples.en: The show ended with a spectacular finale.
examples.cn: 演出以精彩的终场结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: spectacular 源自拉丁语 spectare（观看），表示「壮观的、惊人的」；副词 spectacularly 是「壮观地」，名词 spectacle 是「景象、奇观」，spectator 是「观众」，同根词还有 inspect、respect。

root: 来自拉丁语 spectare（观看），经 spectaculum（表演、景象）进入英语，核心义为值得一看的、景象壮观的，后引申为惊人的。

sensesIntro.en: Spectacular means impressive to see, surprisingly great, or brilliantly performed.
sensesIntro.cn: spectacular 指看上去壮观、大得出人意料，或表演精彩。

core.en: A sight that holds every eye.

branches.en: Fire fills the sky above a river.
branches.cn: 火光充满河面上方的天空。

branches.en: A losing team turns the game around.
branches.cn: 落后的队伍扭转了比赛。

branches.en: The curtain falls on a room full of applause.
branches.cn: 帷幕在满场掌声中落下。

branches.en: A landscape and a stage can both astonish.
branches.cn: 风景与舞台都能令人惊叹。

branches.en: A great result and a great show share one word.
branches.cn: 惊人的成绩与精彩的演出共用一个词。

intro.en: Spectacular connects to the Latin family of watching.
intro.cn: spectacular 与拉丁语中表示观看的词族相连。

latinIntro.en: The roots are spectare, to watch, and spectaculum, a show.
latinIntro.cn: 其词根是 spectare（观看）和 spectaculum（表演）。

items.example: They came to spectate, not to play.
items.exampleCN: 他们是来看比赛的，不是来打的。

definition_en: to guess about something without firm evidence, to think deeply, or to risk money on a possible profit
core_image: 几个人围在桌旁低声讨论一个尚无答案的问题，桌上摊着零散的线索
scene: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
sceneCN: 这里 speculate 是「推测、猜测」（第 1 个义项）；句意：人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。

senses.title: To guess
senses.definition: to form an opinion without firm evidence
senses.definitionCN: 在没有确凿证据的情况下形成看法
senses.example: People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
senses.exampleCN: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。
senses.why: This is the central modern sense of guessing.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代表示猜测的核心含义。

senses.title: To think deeply
senses.definition: to think about a subject in a deep or abstract way
senses.definitionCN: 以深入或抽象的方式思考某一主题
senses.example: The philosopher speculated about the nature of time.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家沉思时间的本质。
senses.why: The older sense names quiet thought rather than guesswork.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的含义指安静的思考，而非猜测。

senses.title: To risk money
senses.definition: to buy something hoping to sell it at a profit
senses.definitionCN: 买进某物，期望以更高价卖出获利
senses.example: He speculated in property and lost money.
senses.exampleCN: 他炒房产赔了钱。
senses.why: A guess about prices turned into a financial gamble.
senses.whyCN: 对价格的猜测，变成了金融上的赌博。

intro.cn: speculate 来自拉丁语 speculari，意为从高处观察。

items.en: Specula meant a watchtower.

abstract.cn: 市场奖励猜测者，惩罚确信者。

abstract.en: A mind that speculates is a mind that is still moving.
abstract.cn: 仍在推测的心，是仍在运动的心。

examples.en: He speculated in property and lost money.

dict_mnemonic.text: speculate 源自拉丁语 speculari（从瞭望塔观察），表示「推测、猜测」，也指「沉思」和「投机」；speculation 是「推测、投机」，speculative 是「推测的、投机性的」，speculator 是「投机者」。

root: 来自拉丁语 speculari（观察、窥探），源于 specula（瞭望塔），本义为从高处远望，后引申为在头脑中推想，再到金融上的投机。

sensesIntro.en: Speculate means to guess without proof, to think deeply, or to risk money on a profit.

branches.cn: 买家押注房价上涨。

branches.en: Guessing and gambling both begin with uncertainty.
branches.cn: 猜测与投机都始于不确定。

branches.en: Idle guessing and deep thought differ only in patience.
branches.cn: 闲猜与深思，只差在耐心。

intro.en: Speculate builds a family of guessing and risking words.
intro.cn: speculate 构成表示猜测与冒险的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is speculari, to observe, from specula, a watchtower.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 speculari（观察），源于 specula（瞭望塔）。

items.example: People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
items.exampleCN: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。

items.example: The paper speculates about a merger.
items.exampleCN: 报纸推测将有一次合并。

items.example: Stop speculating and check the facts.

items.meaning: a guess or a risky deal
a person who gambles on prices
items.exampleCN: 投机者低价买下了土地。

items.example: He spoke speculatively about the cause.
items.exampleCN: 他推测性地谈到了原因。

definition_en: a formal talk given to an audience, or the ability to speak and the words used
core_image: 讲台上一盏台灯照亮演讲稿，台下是一排排安静聆听的面孔
scene: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
sceneCN: 这里 speech 是「演讲」（第 1 个义项）；句意：校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。

senses.title: A formal talk
senses.definition: a formal talk given to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 向听众作的正式讲话
senses.example: The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。
senses.why: This is the most familiar modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最熟悉的含义。

senses.title: The power to speak
senses.definition: the ability to speak, or the act of speaking
senses.definitionCN: 说话的能力或行为
senses.example: Speech develops early in children.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童很早就发展出说话能力。
senses.why: The older sense names the human power itself.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的含义指人类说话的能力本身。

senses.title: Words that are spoken
senses.definition: the words people use and the way they speak
senses.definitionCN: 人们使用的言语及其表达方式
senses.example: The law limits hate speech.
senses.exampleCN: 法律限制仇恨言论。
senses.why: The content of speaking became a public matter.
senses.whyCN: 说话的内容成为公共事务。

intro.en: Speech is an old English word for speaking, related to speak.
intro.cn: speech 是古英语中表示说话的词，与 speak 同源。

items.en: Spræc meant speech, language, or a saying.
items.cn: spræc 意为言语、语言或说法。

items.en: The form became speche.
items.cn: 词形变为 speche。

items.en: Speech named both the power and a formal address.
items.cn: speech 同时指说话能力和正式讲话。

items.en: Freedom of speech made it a political word.
items.cn: freedom of speech 使它成为政治词汇。

items.en: Part of speech named word classes in grammar.
items.cn: part of speech 成为语法中的词类术语。

note.en: Speech is compared with look-alike words and words for talks.
note.cn: 把 speech 与形近词以及表示讲话的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Speech is speaking made public, or the power that makes it possible.
normalIntro.cn: speech 是被公开的说话，或让说话成为可能的能力。

normal.en: The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
normal.cn: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。

normal.en: Speech develops early in children.
normal.cn: 儿童很早就发展出说话能力。

normal.en: The law limits hate speech.
She wrote her speech the night before.
normal.cn: 她前一天晚上写了演讲稿。

normal.en: Freedom of speech is protected by law.

abstract.en: Speech is thought given a body of air.
abstract.cn: 言语是给思想一副空气的身体。

abstract.en: A speech ends, but its echo keeps working.
abstract.cn: 演讲会结束，回声却继续工作。

abstract.en: The right to speak belongs even to those we dislike.
abstract.cn: 说话的权利，也属于我们不喜欢的人。

examples.en: The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
examples.cn: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。

examples.en: Speech develops early in children.
examples.cn: 儿童很早就发展出说话能力。

examples.en: The law limits hate speech.
examples.cn: 法律限制仇恨言论。

dict_mnemonic.text: speech 是古英语 spræc 演变而来，与 speak 同源，指「演讲、言语」；give a speech 是「发表演讲」，freedom of speech 是「言论自由」，part of speech 是「词性」，speechless 是「说不出话的」。

root: 来自古英语 spræc（言语、说话），与 speak 同源，属日耳曼语族，核心义为用词语表达的行为及其公开形式。

sensesIntro.en: Speech means a formal talk, the power to speak, or the words people use.
sensesIntro.cn: speech 指正式演讲、说话能力，或人们使用的言语。

core.en: Words carried into the air for others.
core.cn: 被送进空气、传给别人的词语。

branches.en: A speaker stands before a hall of graduates.
branches.cn: 演讲者站在满堂毕业生面前。

branches.en: A small child forms a first clear sentence.
branches.cn: 小孩说出第一个清晰的句子。

branches.en: A law draws a line around what may be said.
branches.cn: 一条法律为可说的话划出界线。

branches.en: A public address rests on the human power to speak.
branches.cn: 公开演说依赖于人类说话的能力。

branches.en: The ability and its content both carry the name.
branches.cn: 能力与其内容都带着同一个名字。

intro.en: Speech connects to the whole speaking family.
intro.cn: speech 与整个说话词族相连。

latinIntro.en: Speech is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: speech 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The principal gave a speech at the graduation.
items.exampleCN: 校长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。

items.example: He stared speechlessly at the letter.
She spoke softly to the children.
The speaker walked to the podium.
She is speaking on the phone.

items.exampleCN: 战争带来了难以言表的苦难。

definition_en: how fast something moves, the quality of being fast, or to move or make something move faster
core_image: 汽车在空旷的公路上越开越快，路边的标牌向后飞掠成一片模糊
scene: 汽车在高速公路上加速。The car gathered speed on the highway.
sceneCN: 这里 speed 是「速度」（第 1 个义项）；句意：汽车在高速公路上加速。

senses.title: Rate of movement
senses.definition: the rate at which something moves
senses.definitionCN: 某物移动的速率
senses.example: The car gathered speed on the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在高速公路上加速。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词核心的物理含义。

senses.title: The quality of being fast
senses.definition: the quality of moving or acting quickly
senses.definitionCN: 移动或行动迅速的性质
senses.example: She finished the work with great speed.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常迅速地完成了工作。
senses.why: Speed also names quickness itself, not only a number.
senses.whyCN: speed 也指迅速本身，而不只是一个数值。

senses.title: To move fast
senses.definition: to move quickly, or to make something move faster
senses.definitionCN: 快速移动，或使某物移动得更快
senses.example: He sped away on his bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。
senses.why: The verb turns the quality into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这种性质变成动作。

intro.en: Speed first meant success, then quickness, then rate of movement.
intro.cn: speed 最初意为成功，后指迅速，再指移动的速度。

items.en: Sped meant success or prosperity.
items.cn: sped 意为成功或兴旺。

items.en: The word came to mean quickness, as success came fast.
items.cn: 由于成功来得快，这个词开始表示迅速。

items.en: Speed came to mean the rate of motion.
items.cn: speed 开始表示运动的速率。

items.en: Speed limit gave it a legal sense.
items.cn: speed limit 赋予它法律含义。

items.en: To speed up became the common verb of hurrying.
items.cn: speed up 成为常用的催促动词。

note.en: Speed is compared with look-alike words and words for rate.
note.cn: 把 speed 与形近词以及表示速率的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Speed measures how quickly distance is crossed.
normalIntro.cn: speed 衡量距离被越过得多快。

normal.en: The car gathered speed on the highway.
normal.cn: 汽车在高速公路上加速。

normal.en: She finished the work with great speed.
normal.cn: 她非常迅速地完成了工作。

normal.en: He sped away on his bike.
normal.cn: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。

normal.en: The speed limit here is low.
The train reached its top speed.

abstract.en: Speed compresses time into distance.
abstract.cn: 速度把时间压缩成距离。

abstract.en: The faster we move, the less we see.
abstract.cn: 移动得越快，看见的越少。

abstract.en: Hurry is speed without direction.
abstract.cn: 匆忙是没有方向的速度。

examples.en: The car gathered speed on the highway.
examples.cn: 汽车在高速公路上加速。

examples.en: She finished the work with great speed.
examples.cn: 她非常迅速地完成了工作。

examples.en: He sped away on his bike.
examples.cn: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。

dict_mnemonic.text: speed 是「速度、快速」，也可作动词表示「加速」；speed limit 是「限速」，speed up 是「加速」，speedy 是「迅速的」，speedometer 是「速度计」。

root: 来自古英语 sped（成功、顺利），因成功常来得迅速而引申为快速，再指移动速率，动词义为加速、疾驰。

sensesIntro.en: Speed means the rate of movement, quickness, or to move faster.
sensesIntro.cn: speed 指移动速率、迅速，或表示加速。

core.en: Distance divided by the time it takes.

branches.en: A car pushes faster along an open road.
branches.cn: 汽车在开阔公路上越开越快。

branches.en: Hands finish a task before the clock expects.
branches.cn: 双手比时钟预料的更早完成任务。

branches.en: A bicycle rushes past a gate.
branches.cn: 一辆自行车冲过门口。

branches.en: The measure and the hurrying act share one word.
branches.cn: 度量与疾驰的动作共用一个词。

branches.en: Quickness in work and movement both look like speed.
branches.cn: 工作与移动中的迅速都像速度。

intro.en: Speed forms adjectives, adverbs, and measuring devices.
intro.cn: speed 构成形容词、副词和测量装置。

latinIntro.en: Speed is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: speed 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The car gathered speed on the highway.
items.exampleCN: 汽车在高速公路上加速。

items.example: The two cars reached different speeds.
items.exampleCN: 两辆车达到了不同的速度。

items.example: He sped away on his bike.
items.exampleCN: 他骑着自行车疾驰而去。

items.example: They wished her a speedy recovery.
The race was held on a speedway.
items.exampleCN: 比赛在赛车跑道上举行。

definition_en: to write or say the letters of a word in order, or to mean something in a serious way
core_image: 孩子用手指在沙盘上一个字母一个字母地写出自己的名字
scene: 你能拼写你的姓吗？Can you spell your surname?
sceneCN: 这里 spell 是「拼写」（第 1 个义项）；句意：你能拼写你的姓吗？

senses.title: To write letters
senses.definition: to write or say the letters of a word in the correct order
senses.definitionCN: 按正确顺序写出或说出单词的字母
senses.example: Can you spell your surname?
senses.exampleCN: 你能拼写你的姓吗？
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of letters in order.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示按顺序排列字母的含义。

senses.title: To say letters aloud
senses.definition: to say the letters of a word one by one
senses.definitionCN: 逐个说出单词的字母
senses.example: The teacher spelled the word aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把这个词逐个字母读了出来。
senses.why: The voice can spell as well as the hand.
senses.whyCN: 嘴和手一样都能拼。

senses.title: To mean trouble
senses.definition: to suggest that something, often bad, will happen
senses.definitionCN: 暗示某事（常为坏事）将会发生
senses.example: Dark clouds spell rain.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云意味着要下雨。
senses.why: Letters that form a word foretell its meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拼成词的字母，预告了它的含义。

intro.en: Spell came through French from a Germanic word for a story or saying.
intro.cn: spell 经法语来自日耳曼语中表示故事或说法的词。

items.en: A word for a tale or saying lay behind spell.
items.cn: 表示故事或说法的词是 spell 的源头。

items.en: Espeller meant to tell or recite letters.
items.cn: espeller 意为讲述或读出字母。

items.en: Spell entered English meaning to read letter by letter.
items.cn: spell 以逐字母读出之义进入英语。

items.en: It came to mean writing words correctly.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示正确写出单词。

items.en: To spell trouble used the word for foretelling.
items.cn: spell trouble 借用了预示的含义。

note.en: Spell is compared with look-alike words and verbs of writing and meaning.
note.cn: 把 spell 与形近词以及表示书写和意味的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to look at and understand words

normalIntro.en: To spell is to line letters up until they make a word.
normalIntro.cn: spell 就是把字母排好队，直到成为一个词。

normal.en: Can you spell your surname?
The teacher spelled the word aloud.
normal.cn: 老师把这个词逐个字母读了出来。

normal.en: Dark clouds spell rain.
Please spell out your full name.
He often misspells difficult words.

abstract.en: Letters obey an order or they mean nothing.
abstract.cn: 字母遵守顺序，否则毫无意义。

abstract.en: A name is held together by how it is spelled.
abstract.cn: 一个名字靠它的拼法维系。

abstract.en: To spell is to trust that order creates meaning.
abstract.cn: 拼写，就是相信顺序能创造意义。

examples.en: Can you spell your surname?
examples.cn: 你能拼写你的姓吗？

examples.en: The teacher spelled the word aloud.
examples.cn: 老师把这个词逐个字母读了出来。

examples.en: Dark clouds spell rain.
examples.cn: 乌云意味着要下雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: spell 是「拼写」，也可指「逐字母读出」和「意味着」；spelling 是「拼写、拼法」，misspell 是「拼错」，spell out 是「拼出、明确说明」，spell trouble 是「意味着麻烦」。

root: 来自古法语 espeller，源于日耳曼语中表示讲述、说法的词，核心义为按顺序说出或写出字母，后引申为预示、意味着。

sensesIntro.en: Spell means to write letters in order, to say them aloud, or to mean something bad.
sensesIntro.cn: spell 指按顺序写出字母、逐字母读出，或意味着不好的结果。

core.en: Letters lined up into meaning.

branches.en: A child writes her name in sand.
branches.cn: 孩子在沙上写出自己的名字。

branches.en: A teacher pronounces each letter slowly.
branches.cn: 老师慢慢读出每个字母。

branches.en: Grey clouds gather over a field.
branches.cn: 灰云在田野上空聚集。

branches.en: Hand and voice both put letters in order.
branches.cn: 手和嘴都把字母按顺序排列。

branches.en: Arranged letters and gathering clouds both announce a meaning.
branches.cn: 排好的字母与聚集的云都在宣告含义。

intro.en: Spell forms nouns and verbs of letters and mistakes.
intro.cn: spell 构成表示字母和错误的动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Spell came through French from Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: spell 经法语来自日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.exampleCN: 他慢慢拼出了自己的名字。

items.example: The word was spelt with two letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个词用了两个字母拼写。

items.meaning: the act or way of spelling
items.example: Check the spelling of the name.

definition_en: to use money to buy things, to pass time in a place or way, or to use up energy
core_image: 收银台上硬币一枚枚被推出去，旁边日历上的日子也一页页翻过
scene: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
sceneCN: 这里 spend 是「度过」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他们在海边度过了整个周末。

senses.title: To pay out money
senses.definition: to use money to buy something
senses.definitionCN: 用钱购买东西
senses.example: She spent fifty pounds on the coat.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了五十英镑买那件大衣。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最常见的含义。

senses.title: To pass time
senses.definition: to pass time in a particular way or place
senses.definitionCN: 以特定方式或在特定地点度过时间
senses.example: They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。
senses.why: Time is treated like money that is paid out.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作花出去的钱。

senses.title: To use up energy
senses.definition: to use up energy or effort on something
senses.definitionCN: 在某事上耗尽精力或努力
senses.example: He spent all his energy on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 他把全部精力都花在这个项目上。
senses.why: Energy can be spent like money and time.
senses.whyCN: 精力也能像金钱和时间一样被花掉。

intro.en: Spend came from Latin expendere, to weigh out money, through Old English.
intro.cn: spend 经古英语来自拉丁语 expendere，意为称出钱来支付。

items.en: Expendere meant to weigh out and pay money.
items.cn: expendere 意为称出并支付钱款。

items.en: Spendan meant to pay out or use up.
items.cn: spendan 意为支付或耗尽。

items.en: Spend came to mean passing time as well.
items.cn: spend 也开始表示度过时间。

items.en: Spending became the word for household costs.
items.cn: spending 成为表示家庭开支的词。

items.en: Spend energy extended it beyond money.
items.cn: spend energy 把它扩展到金钱之外。

note.en: Spend is compared with look-alike words and verbs of using resources.
note.cn: 把 spend 与形近词以及表示使用资源的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to go through a period of time

normalIntro.en: To spend is to let something valuable flow out of your hands.
normalIntro.cn: spend 就是让有价值的东西从手中流走。

normal.en: They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
normal.cn: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。

normal.en: She spent fifty pounds on the coat.
normal.cn: 她花了五十英镑买那件大衣。

normal.en: He spent all his energy on the project.
normal.cn: 他把全部精力都花在这个项目上。

normal.en: We spent the night in a small hotel.
normal.cn: 我们在一家小旅馆过夜。

normal.en: Learn to spend wisely.

abstract.en: Time is the only currency no one can earn back.
abstract.cn: 时间是人唯一赚不回来的货币。

abstract.en: What we spend shows what we value.
abstract.cn: 我们把钱花在哪，就说明我们看重什么。

abstract.en: A day spent well is never a payment.
abstract.cn: 过得好的一天，从来不是一笔支出。

examples.en: They spent the whole weekend at the beach.
examples.cn: 他们在海边度过了整个周末。

examples.en: She spent fifty pounds on the coat.
examples.cn: 她花了五十英镑买那件大衣。

examples.en: He spent all his energy on the project.
examples.cn: 他把全部精力都花在这个项目上。

dict_mnemonic.text: spend 源自拉丁语 expendere（称出钱款），表示「花费」，也可指「度过时间」和「消耗精力」；spending 是「开支」，spender 是「花钱的人」，spendthrift 是「挥霍者」。

root: 来自拉丁语 expendere（称量、支付），经古英语 spendan 进入英语，核心义为付出金钱，后扩展到时间与精力的消耗。

sensesIntro.en: Spend means to pay out money, to pass time, or to use up energy.
sensesIntro.cn: spend 指付出金钱、度过时间，或消耗精力。

core.en: Letting valuable things flow away.

branches.en: Coins cross a counter into another hand.
branches.cn: 硬币越过柜台，进入另一只手。

branches.en: A family walks the shore until evening.
branches.cn: 一家人沿着海岸走到傍晚。

branches.en: A worker pours the last of his strength into a task.
branches.cn: 工人把最后的力气投进工作。

branches.en: Money and time are both counted out and given away.
branches.cn: 金钱与时间都被数着交出去。

branches.en: Time and energy pass through the same open hand.
branches.cn: 时间与精力穿过同一只张开的手。

intro.en: Spend forms nouns for money use and for people.
intro.cn: spend 构成表示用钱和用钱者的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is expendere, to weigh out and pay.

definition_en: to turn round quickly, to make thread, or to invent a story
core_image: 陀螺在地面上飞快旋转

senses.title: Turn round fast

senses.title: Invent a tale

senses.exampleCN: 他编了一个关于失落之城的故事。

intro.en: Spin is an Old English verb for drawing out thread.
intro.cn: spin 是古英语动词，指把纤维抽成线。

items.en: Spinnan meant to draw out thread.

She spins wool into thread.
The spider spins a web.

senses.title: The inner self

senses.title: Mood or morale

senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体的情绪与士气

definition_zh: 恶意；怨恨；不顾（in spite of）
definition_en: a wish to hurt or annoy someone; in spite of means despite
core_image: 一双冷冷盯着人的眼睛
scene: 尽管下雨，他们还是出发了。They set off in spite of the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 spite 是「不顾、尽管」（第 3 个义项）；句意：尽管下雨，他们还是出发了。

senses.title: Wish to hurt
senses.definition: a desire to hurt or annoy another person
senses.definitionCN: 想伤害或惹恼别人的心思
senses.example: He broke the vase out of spite.
senses.exampleCN: 他出于恶意打碎了花瓶。
senses.why: The core sense is small, active ill will.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的义项，指主动的小恶意。

senses.title: Lasting resentment
senses.definition: a lasting feeling of resentment
senses.definitionCN: 持续不散的怨恨情绪
senses.example: There was spite in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音里带着怨气。
senses.why: The feeling is seen as stored rather than acted out.
senses.whyCN: 这种情绪被看作积存的，而非当下发作。

senses.title: Despite
senses.definition: used in the phrase in spite of, meaning despite
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in spite of，意为尽管、不顾
senses.example: They set off in spite of the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，他们还是出发了。
senses.why: The phrase turns ill will into resistance to a fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把恶意转化为对事实的抗拒。

intro.en: Spite comes from Old French despit, meaning contempt.
intro.cn: spite 来自古法语 despit，意为轻蔑。

items.en: Despectus meant a looking down on others.
items.cn: despectus 意为俯视、轻视。

items.en: Despit named contempt and ill will.
items.cn: despit 指轻蔑与恶意。

items.en: Spite entered English as a word for malice.
items.cn: spite 以「恶意」之义进入英语。

items.en: In spite of came to mean despite.
items.cn: in spite of 逐渐表示「尽管」。

items.en: Spiteful described a person full of ill will.
items.cn: spiteful 形容满怀恶意的人。

note.en: Spite is compared with look-alike words and words for ill will.
note.cn: 把 spite 与形近词以及表示恶意的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spite is anger kept for later.

normal.en: He did it out of spite.
She spoke with spite.
We went out in spite of the rain.
normal.cn: 尽管下雨我们还是出去了。

normal.en: Don't act out of spite.
Spite made him refuse the offer.
normal.cn: 赌气让他拒绝了那个提议。

abstract.en: Spite drinks its own poison first.
abstract.cn: 怨恨先喝下自己的毒药。

abstract.en: In spite of the rain, the road still leads on.
abstract.cn: 尽管下雨，路仍向前。

abstract.en: Small malice leaves the longest marks.
abstract.cn: 小小的恶意，留下最长的痕迹。

examples.en: He broke the vase out of spite.

examples.cn: 她的声音里带着怨气。

examples.en: They set off in spite of the rain.
examples.cn: 尽管下雨，他们还是出发了。

dict_mnemonic.text: spite 是「恶意」，out of spite 是「出于恶意」；in spite of 是固定短语，意为「尽管」，相当于 despite；spiteful 是形容词「恶意的」。

root: 来自拉丁语 despectus（轻视），经古法语 despit 进入英语，核心义为「轻蔑带来的恶意」，短语 in spite of 又发展出「尽管」。

sensesIntro.en: Spite means petty ill will, stored resentment, or, in in spite of, despite.
sensesIntro.cn: spite 指小恶意、积存的怨恨，或在 in spite of 中表示尽管。

core.en: Contempt turned into a small weapon.
core.cn: 轻蔑变成的一件小武器。

branches.en: A hand breaks what it cannot have.
branches.cn: 得不到的手，干脆把它打碎。

branches.en: An old insult is kept warm.
branches.cn: 旧日的冒犯被一直焐着。

branches.en: Rain falls, yet the walk goes on.
branches.cn: 雨在下，脚步却没有停。

branches.en: Malice and memory feed each other.
branches.cn: 恶意与记忆，互相喂养。

branches.en: Resentment hardens into refusal.
branches.cn: 怨恨硬化成了抗拒。

intro.en: Spite forms adjectives, adverbs, and nouns.

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is despectus, a looking down.

definition_en: very impressive and beautiful, or excellent
core_image: 夕阳把整片山谷染成金色
scene: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。The sunset made the valley splendid.
sceneCN: 这里 splendid 是「壮丽的、辉煌的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。

senses.title: Magnificent to see
senses.definition: magnificent and impressive to look at
senses.definitionCN: 看上去宏伟而令人赞叹的
senses.example: The sunset made the valley splendid.
senses.exampleCN: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。
senses.why: The core sense comes from shining beauty.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的义项源于光彩夺目的美。

senses.title: Very good
senses.definition: excellent, used especially in spoken praise
senses.definitionCN: 极好的，多用于口头称赞
senses.example: That is a splendid idea.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个绝妙的主意。
senses.why: The visual sense weakens into general praise.
senses.whyCN: 视觉义弱化，变成一般性的称赞。

senses.title: Rich in style
senses.definition: rich and impressive in style or decoration
senses.definitionCN: 风格或装饰富丽堂皇的
senses.example: The hall had a splendid ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅有一个华丽的天花板。
senses.why: The sense stays visual but moves to built things.
senses.whyCN: 仍属视觉义，但转向人造之物。

intro.en: Splendid comes from Latin splendidus, meaning shining.
intro.cn: splendid 来自拉丁语 splendidus，意为闪光的。

items.en: Splendere meant to shine or glow.
items.cn: splendere 意为发光、闪耀。

items.en: Splendidus described something bright and fine.
items.cn: splendidus 形容明亮而精美之物。

items.en: Splendid entered English as shining and fine.
items.cn: splendid 以「明亮精美」之义进入英语。

items.en: It broadened to mean magnificent.
items.cn: 词义扩展为「宏伟壮丽」。

items.en: It also became a polite word of praise.
items.cn: 它又成为礼貌的称赞用语。

note.en: Splendid is compared with look-alike words and words for beauty.
note.cn: 把 splendid 与形近词以及表示华美的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Splendid is light made into a compliment.

normal.en: What a splendid view!
That is a splendid idea.
They live in a splendid house.
normal.cn: 他们住在一座华丽的房子里。

normal.en: The garden looks splendid in spring.
normal.cn: 春天的花园看起来美极了。

normal.en: You did a splendid job.

abstract.en: Splendour is a light that stays after sunset.
abstract.cn: 辉煌，是日落之后仍留着的光。

abstract.en: Praise borrows the words of sunlight.
abstract.cn: 赞美借用了阳光的词汇。

abstract.en: The finest halls are quiet inside.
abstract.cn: 最华丽的厅堂，内里最安静。

examples.en: The sunset made the valley splendid.
examples.cn: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。

examples.en: That is a splendid idea.
examples.cn: 那是个绝妙的主意。

examples.en: The hall had a splendid ceiling.

root: 来自拉丁语 splendidus（闪光的），词根 splendere 意为发光，核心义由「光彩夺目」扩展到「壮丽」与「极好」。

sensesIntro.en: Splendid means magnificent to see, excellent, or rich in style.

core.en: Light that makes people stop and look.

branches.en: Gold spreads over the valley.
branches.cn: 金色铺满山谷。

branches.en: A voice says, what a good idea.
branches.cn: 一个声音说，这主意真好。

branches.en: Carved ceilings catch the candlelight.
branches.cn: 雕花天花板接住烛光。

branches.en: Nature and craft both aim at glory.
branches.cn: 自然与工艺，都朝着辉煌。

branches.en: Praise and ornament share one brightness.
branches.cn: 赞美与装饰，共用一种明亮。

intro.en: Splendid forms comparison, nouns, and adverbs.
intro.cn: splendid 构成比较级、名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is splendere, to shine.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 splendere，意为发光。

items.example: The view grew splendider at dusk.

definition_en: to divide or break into parts
core_image: 斧头落下，木柴裂成两半
scene: 他把木头劈成两半。He split the wood in two.
sceneCN: 这里 split 是「劈开」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把木头劈成两半。

senses.title: Break apart
senses.definition: to divide or break something along a line
senses.definitionCN: 沿一条线把某物分开或劈断
senses.example: He split the wood in two.
senses.exampleCN: 他把木头劈成两半。
senses.why: The core sense is a physical break.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的义项是物理上的断开。

senses.title: Divide into groups
senses.definition: to divide into separate groups or parts
senses.definitionCN: 分裂成不同的群体或部分

senses.title: Share the cost

senses.example: We split the bill between us.

items.cn: 词义从木头扩展到群体与金钱。

items.en: Split second named a tiny division of time.
items.cn: split second 指极短的一瞬。
